researcher_notes: This category came back thinner and more mixed than prior Phase 2 batches, consistent with the brief's expectation that robotics-in-restaurants is still an emerging, pilot-heavy space. Of the 5 assigned vendors, only 2 (Miso Robotics, Picnic) produced a reasonable set of dated, named RESTAURANT-BRAND customer relationships; Nala Robotics produced exactly one (a convenience-store/gas-station chain, borderline fit); and both Chef Robotics and Mashgin came back with essentially no qualifying restaurant-CHAIN evidence despite being large, well-documented, well-funded companies -- their named customer bases sit in adjacent categories (food manufacturing/meal-kit production for Chef Robotics; convenience stores, stadiums, airports and corporate cafeterias for Mashgin) rather than restaurant brands operating consumer-facing locations. Two corporate-structure findings stand out: (1) Picnic (the pizza-assembly robotics vendor) shut down entirely on 2026-05-11, filing a General Assignment for the Benefit of Creditors and liquidating its assets to a buyer identified only as 'CMBG' (GeekWire, 2026-05-26) -- flagged below as defunct. (2) Miso Robotics remains operating and has actually expanded its footprint in 2026 (acquired workforce-intelligence platform Zignyl and the IP/patent portfolio of defunct rival Zume), but its public SEC Regulation A/D filings show it has run on thin, investor-financing-dependent margins for years (cash of $9.8M at end of FY2025) -- it is not defunct but should not be read as financially secure. On discontinued deployments specifically: Chipotle's 'Chippy' tortilla-chip robot (piloted with Miso starting March 2022) was abandoned -- then-CEO Brian Niccol said on the record in March 2024 that 'Chippy didn't pan out the way we thought it would,' and Chipotle's subsequent robotics investment (Autocado, an avocado-processing robot) is a separate, non-Miso system. Separately, a skeptical trade-press piece from January 2025 (Restaurant Dive) directly undercuts the more triumphant Miso/White Castle press releases: despite a February 2022 press release announcing plans to install Flippy 2 in '100 new locations,' Miso 'had only installed the robotic arm in 13 restaurants across the two brands' (White Castle and Jack in the Box combined) as of that January 2025 reporting date -- a real, sourced example of the gap between robotics-partnership PR and actual installed footprint that the task brief asked us to watch for. The Cali Group/Miso/PopID joint-venture concept restaurant 'CaliExpress by Flippy' (Pasadena) was NOT written as a customer record because Miso co-owns that venture rather than selling to an independent restaurant-brand customer; its current operating status is itself ambiguous in public sources (Yelp lists it 'temporarily closed' with a placeholder 2035 reopen date, and at least one 2024 account describes it as having been a seasonal pop-up), so it should be treated as a discontinued/paused pilot, not an active deployment, if it is ever referenced elsewhere in RB.

records.confidence_rationale: Multi-year, multi-stage relationship with dated press releases at each stage, corroborated by an independent January 2025 trade-press report giving an actual installed-unit count rather than relying only on promotional press releases.
records.notes: Longest-running, best-documented relationship in this category. Pilot began September 2020 (single Chicagoland location); White Castle announced intent to expand to up to 10 locations in October 2020 (PR Newswire); a further press release on 2022-02-15 announced plans to install Flippy 2 in '100 new locations.' However, per this January 2025 Restaurant Dive reporting, actual installed footprint was only 13 restaurants COMBINED across White Castle and Jack in the Box as of that date -- well short of the '100 locations' framing from the 2022 press release. A subsequent March 2026 Fast Casual piece (see Insert Coin record) says Flippy has 'surpassed 5 million fried baskets' and reached 'seven U.S. states' including White Castle, but still gives no confirmed total unit count. Wrote deployment_status as multi_unit_deployment (not brand_wide/enterprise_wide) because no source confirms full-chain completion at a stated count; White Castle operates 350+ locations system-wide, so even the higher-end characterizations describe a small minority of the chain.

records.confidence_rationale: Jack in the Box's own investor-relations newsroom announced the pilot with a specific date and product names; a 2024 SEC filing (per secondary reporting) and the January 2025 Restaurant Dive piece both confirm it was still active/ongoing, still scoped as a pilot.
records.notes: Pilot began at a single San Diego location testing Flippy 2 (burger-flipping arm) and Sippy (drink dispensing). Per the January 2025 Restaurant Dive report, this pilot -- combined with White Castle's -- accounted for only 13 total installed locations as of that date. No source found confirming expansion beyond pilot scope.

records.confidence_rationale: Multiple dated trade-press pieces confirm the test existed, but testing began at Inspire Brands' innovation center/ghost kitchen rather than a live guest-facing Buffalo Wild Wings restaurant, and no later source was found confirming it ever reached a standalone restaurant.
records.notes: Product is 'Flippy Wings,' a robotic wing fryer. Testing began fall 2021 at the Inspire Brands Innovation Center in Atlanta, with a stated plan to move into Inspire's ghost kitchen ('Alliance Kitchen') before eventual installation in a standalone Buffalo Wild Wings restaurant. No subsequent press release or trade-press coverage was found confirming that final step occurred -- treat this as an unconfirmed/possibly-never-completed pilot, brand is Inspire Brands' Buffalo Wild Wings concept specifically (not other Inspire brands).

records.confidence_rationale: Both the original pilot announcement (Chipotle's own newsroom) and its discontinuation (on-the-record quote from then-CEO Brian Niccol) are independently, specifically sourced and dated.
records.notes: 'Chippy,' an autonomous tortilla-chip-making robot, was piloted starting March 2022 at Chipotle's Cultivate Center (Irvine, CA) and at least one Southern California restaurant. Then-CEO Brian Niccol confirmed on the record in a March 2024 Yahoo Finance Q&A that 'Chippy didn't pan out the way we thought it would.' Chipotle's next kitchen-robotics investment, 'Autocado' (avocado processing, launched ~July 2023), is a separate, non-Miso system -- do not conflate the two vendors if Autocado is researched separately for this graph.

records.confidence_rationale: Well-sourced, dated press release with specific commitment language, but the commitment itself is forward-looking (future new-store builds) rather than a confirmed current deployment, and no later source was found quantifying how many locations actually went live.
records.notes: Wing Zone committed to specifying Flippy 2 (wing fryer) into the standard build of all FUTURE restaurant locations (100+ then in its development pipeline at announcement time) -- described in coverage as the first fast-casual brand to spec food robotics into its operations at this level. This is a forward construction-standard commitment, not a confirmation that any stated number of restaurants are currently operating with Flippy. A March 2026 Fast Casual piece (see Insert Coin record) lists Wing Zone among Miso's current named brands but gives no unit count, so treat the deployment as ongoing but unquantified.

records.confidence_rationale: Well-sourced, dated launch announcement for a single named test location/program, but no later source found confirming expansion beyond the initial test.
records.notes: CookRight Coffee is an AI-camera/sensor system (not a physical robot) that monitors coffee volume, temperature and freshness and alerts staff when to brew a new batch -- classified as computer_vision rather than robotics_autonomous_systems since it doesn't physically manipulate anything. Panera began testing the system in April 2022. No subsequent source found confirming broader rollout beyond the initial pilot; status not reconfirmed.

records.confidence_rationale: Only a single passing trade-press mention found (no dedicated press release), naming the brand but giving no location count, deployment date, or scope detail.
records.notes: Insert Coin is a small Washington-state restaurant chain named alongside White Castle, Jack in the Box and Wing Zone as a Flippy deployment site in this March 2026 update on Miso's cumulative basket count (5M+) and geographic footprint (7 states). No dedicated press release or additional detail found; included for completeness given the explicit named mention, but this is thin evidence and should be treated as provisional.

records.confidence_rationale: Named, dated vendor press release describing a specific multi-location artisanal-pizza chain's use of the Picnic Pizza Station across its restaurants and at stadium pop-ups.
records.notes: Moto Pizza is a Seattle-area artisanal pizza chain (3 brick-and-mortar locations as of the announcement, plus stadium/high-volume event use, e.g., at Seattle sports venues) that named its Picnic robot 'Otis.' IMPORTANT: Picnic (the vendor) shut down entirely on 2026-05-11 (General Assignment for the Benefit of Creditors, assets liquidated) -- see vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_renamed. Current status of Moto Pizza's robot equipment/support post-shutdown is unknown and was not found in any source; treat this relationship as historical as of the vendor's 2026 closure even though it was presumably still active up to that point.

records.confidence_rationale: Named, dated press releases exist on both the initial partnership and a specific ($800M / 5,000-unit) deal, but Speedy Eats itself disclosed on its own crowdfunding page that it was 'pre-revenue' with only a 'working prototype' at the time, and only one physical location (Baton Rouge, opened 2023) was ever confirmed built.
records.notes: Speedy Eats (Bancroft Automated Restaurant Services / BARS Inc., Baton Rouge) is an emerging unstaffed drive-thru concept, not an established restaurant chain -- initial partnership announced 2022-06-02, followed by this $800M/5,000-location projected-volume deal announced 2022-08-05. Highly promotional, forward-looking numbers ($800M value, 5,000 units over 5 years, 40,000 target parking-lot sites) far exceed anything confirmed built: only one Speedy Eats location (Baton Rouge, opened 2023) was found confirmed in operation. Additionally, Picnic itself shut down 2026-05-11 (see vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_renamed), so this relationship should be read as defunct/lapsed regardless of Speedy Eats' own trajectory. Recommend Low-to-Medium confidence treatment in the graph given the gap between deal-value framing and actual built footprint.

records.confidence_rationale: Named, dated press release (BusinessWire) with specific product and rollout-plan detail, but the vendor's own headline framing ('at All Locations') is more absolute than the release's body text, which describes a phased rollout plan with a modest store count at announcement time.
records.notes: Re-Up bills itself as an 'AI-powered convenience store and gas station' chain that deploys Nala's 'The Wingman' autonomous fryer to prepare fried chicken/fries. IMPORTANT CATEGORY-FIT CAVEAT: Re-Up is fundamentally a convenience-store/fuel-retail chain with an attached food-service program, not a traditional standalone restaurant brand -- flagging this for Todd's judgment on whether it belongs in the restaurant-brand graph at all. Deployment scope: at announcement, Re-Up had only 9 c-stores open, with a stated goal of 25-30 more by end of 2024 and 200+ eventually; the press-release HEADLINE says 'at All Locations' but the body describes a forward rollout plan rather than a completed one, so deployment_status is written as active_rollout rather than all_location_deployment despite the headline's own framing -- a direct example of the 'be skeptical of headline scaling language' guidance in the task brief.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: Chef Robotics -- NO qualifying restaurant-brand evidence found. Chef Robotics is a real, well-funded (Series A $43.1M, March 2025), actively growing company (TechCrunch, April 2026, described it as 'thriving'), but every named customer with a public case study (Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice, Chef Bombay) is a food MANUFACTURER or meal-kit/prepared-meal producer selling into grocery/retail distribution, not a restaurant chain operating consumer-facing dine-in/QSR locations. The company's own materials describe QSR/fast-casual entry as a still-future goal ('partnered six large-scale commissary hubs... will soon enable it to enter fast casual and QSR kitchens' -- future tense as of the sources checked), and it separately says it serves an unnamed large school-lunch provider and an unnamed large airline caterer, neither disclosed publicly. Recommend not promoting any Chef Robotics record into the graph from this batch.

Mashgin -- effectively no qualifying evidence for genuine restaurant-CHAIN customers. Mashgin is large and well-documented (1.5B+ transactions, 5,000+ deployment locations, $62.5M raised) but its named, dated deployments are overwhelmingly convenience stores (Circle K/Couche-Tard, 7,000+ stores, PR dated 2022-06-02 -- included above as a borderline record for Todd's review only, not a confident restaurant-chain fit), sports stadiums (e.g., Denver Broncos concessions), airports, and corporate/hospital cafeterias run by contract foodservice firms (Aramark, Compass Group). No dated, named traditional QSR/fast-casual/full-service restaurant BRAND customer was found in any search performed for this batch.
vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: Picnic (pizza assembly robotics) -- CONFIRMED DEFUNCT. Shut down 2026-05-11 via a General Assignment for the Benefit of Creditors; assets liquidated to a buyer identified in press coverage only as Los Angeles firm 'CMBG' (GeekWire, published 2026-05-26; also covered by Nation's Restaurant News). Founded 2016, raised roughly $50M+ lifetime. Its own shutdown coverage explicitly lists several category peers as also already defunct: Piestro, Basil Street, Zume Pizza, and Chowbotics -- none of which were in this batch's assigned vendor list, but worth flagging for Todd in case any appear in a future vendor-universe pass, since the pattern (well-funded, well-covered robotics-pizza startups quietly failing) is now well-evidenced across at least five companies in this sub-space.
